gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-nastaliq-urd: Grandstander draws every stroke like a neon tube, bold and expressive, with letters held open and a tall x-height. And Noto Nastaliq Urdu, a classic serif, brings dignified editorial polish, its hairlines present but never razor thin.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Expressive and loud, Grandstander keeps its line thickness in a gentle monotone, every stroke the same easygoing width. But Noto Rashi Hebrew feels like lightly engraved brass beside it, bookish, with thin strokes that stay sturdy and thick ones held back.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Chunky, playful shapes with no heavy-to-light shift. Grandstander sets the tone, and Noto Serif Ahom answers in a tall, lofty lowercase whose diagonals run slightly lighter than its verticals, giving the page a dignified counterweight.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-armeni: Rounded, drawn-with-one-pen letters from Grandstander sit over a body with big open counters and a mild, approachable stroke contrast. Noto Serif Armenian supplies the visible thick-thin variation.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-baline: Fat, friendly, hairline-free lettering up top. Grandstander never lets a thin line sit against a thick stem, while Noto Serif Balinese shifts its stroke widths just enough to notice, and its lowercase stands tall.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-bengal: Noto Serif Bengali is refined and editorial, with slightly thinner hairlines. Grandstander's pen line holds one width throughout, so a long passage in the Bengali body would feel like a gentle thick-to-thin shift underneath a bold, steady headline.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-devana: Noto Serif Devanagari reads like a literary classic serif, with slightly thinner curves atop its rounded letters and a big lowercase body. And Grandstander's plain constant-width lines make the weight change along each body stroke the pair's strongest single quality.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-dives-: Grandstander's monoline stroke runs start to finish, bold and expressive with a tall x-height. Noto Serif Dives Akuru reads softly, a faint pull between heavy verticals and lighter horizontals.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Grandstander has the weight of a drawn wire, bold and expressive in every line. But Noto Serif Dogra, a text serif, takes the quieter job, its curves thickening slightly like a reed pen, with capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-ethiop: Straight-edged, constant strokes, bold and bouncy. Grandstander is the loud half, and Noto Serif Ethiopic gives the strongest quality of the pair back as a classic bookish texture, with words forming solid blocks and gentle weight variation.
